findings.title: The drift guard only sees serialized hit keys, so a new ScoredHit field marked #[serde(skip)] can be left unclassified with no test failure
findings.evidence: read_explain_guard_tests.rs:199 builds the sweep input as `keys(&serde_json::to_value(&hit).expect("serialize full hit"))` and read_explain_guard_tests.rs:213-224 iterates only that set, so a field that serde never emits is invisible to the guard. Verified by independent mutation in an isolated git worktree: adding `drift_probe: Option<String>` with `#[serde(skip)]` to crates/clio-retrieve/src/types.rs, naming it `drift_probe: _` in the exhaustive pattern at read_explain.rs:114-125, and setting it in the `full_hit()` fixture left `cargo test -p clio-mcp --locked --lib read_explain` at '6 passed; 0 failed'. The same field WITHOUT `#[serde(skip)]` and left unclassified produced 'test result: FAILED. 5 passed; 1 failed' with 'hit key `drift_probe` is unclassified: add it to TRACE_HIT_KEYS if it belongs in the trace, or to an exclusion set with a reason'. Practical impact is small: a serde-skipped field cannot reach the wire, so it cannot leak content into the trace. What drifts is the declared classification record, and read_explain.rs:49-51 claims 'production code enforces the same classification at compile time through the exhaustive pattern', which is false: the pattern only forces a field to be *mentioned*, and `newfield: _` satisfies it.
findings.requirement_ref: phase doc §5 Task 1 'Adding a new hit field either appears in the trace (if PII-safe and listed) or is excluded (if content-derived), by deliberate choice in one place'; §8 T100740-03; §12 'Any future hit field is deliberately classified as trace-visible or content-excluded'; AGENTS.md header/ownership accuracy rule
findings.recommendation: Sweep struct field names instead of serialized keys: add a `..`-free destructuring inside the guard test that binds every field of `ScoredHit` and of the flattened `RetrieveHit` by name, then assert `classify(name).is_some()` for each bound name. The compiler then makes the name list exhaustive, so a `#[serde(skip)]` field is covered and the test fails on an unclassified field. Separately, correct read_explain.rs:49-51 to say the pattern enforces field-mention (with the test enforcing classification), and add a test that fails if `..` or a wildcard is reintroduced into the `explain_hit` pattern.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED (r1 attempt rejected by the remedy approver; mechanism replaced in remediation r2). r1 swept struct field names, but the exhaustive destructuring and the swept name list were two independent hand-written blocks, so a #[serde(skip)] field mentioned in explain_hit and left out of the vec![] still passed (approver measured '6 passed; 0 failed'). Remediation r2 makes one artifact serve both lists: hit_field_names is now generated from one shared macro_rules! declaration in read_explain_guard_tests.rs (with_hit_fields! declares every ScoredHit and flattened RetrieveHit field exactly once; make_hit_field_names! expands that single list to BOTH the '..'-free destructuring (field: _ bindings) and vec![stringify!(field), ...]), so the compiler forces every field through the one list and the sweep forces every listed field to be classified. Re-verified with the approver's exact mutation after the fix: #[serde(skip)] drift_probe: Option<String> on ScoredHit (types.rs), initialized in finalize.rs, named drift_probe: _ in explain_hit, set in the fixture -> 'cargo test -p clio-mcp --locked --lib read_explain' FAILS to compile at the macro-generated destructuring (read_explain_guard_tests.rs:178). rustc diagnostic note: for macro-expanded patterns the missing field reports as 'pattern requires `..` due to inaccessible fields' (the sibling of error[E0027], which a hand-written control pattern in the same compilation did report naming drift_probe); both are hard compile errors, so the forcing function holds either way. Control mutation (drift_probe declared in the shared list as well, left unclassified): 'test result: FAILED. 5 passed; 1 failed' with 'the swept field names and the serialized keys diverged' (read_explain_guard_tests.rs:275). Both mutations reverted from saved copies; grep -rn drift_probe crates -> 0 hits; suite green again '6 passed; 0 failed'. The false claim at read_explain.rs:49-51 was removed (see F-05). The '..'-reintroduction guard is covered by evidence: with '..' in the explain_hit pattern and 'scores' classified TraceVisible (simulating a dropped field), 3 tests fail incl. 'classification and projection disagree for `scores`' and the wire assertion; '..' alone compiles and passes only because nothing trace-visible is dropped today. Mutation reverted.

findings.title: The phase's required end-to-end trace test does not exist, the §9 evidence calls an in-process dispatch the real MCP binding, and the whole §8 Required Tests checklist is left unticked
findings.evidence: phase doc §8 lists '- [ ] End-to-end tests (real MCP `retrieve` with `explain`)' and phase doc §9 AC-100740-01 describes the wire test as asserting the key set 'through the real MCP `retrieve` binding'. The three wire tests actually call the in-process dispatcher: read_explain_tests.rs:167, read_explain_tests.rs:222 and read_explain_tests.rs:264 all invoke `crate::write_tools::dispatch(&state, "retrieve", &json!({... "explain": true ...}))` with no JSON-RPC frame, no transport, and no `McpHandler`. The only real-transport `retrieve ... explain:true` call in the repo is the pre-existing fixture at crates/clio-mcp/tests/mcp_read_transport_conformance.rs:44-47 (mirrored over HTTP through the same fixture list), and that test asserts only masked transport parity, never the trace key set. The §8 checklist is still `- [ ]` for all seven categories and the 'Required Test Scenarios' table has no result column, while phase doc §9 and the 'Definition of Done' checkbox 'Required tests pass' both claim the tests pass.
findings.requirement_ref: phase doc §8 'Required Tests' and 'Required Test Scenarios'; §9 AC-100740-01 evidence; 'Definition of Done' checkbox 'Required tests pass'
findings.recommendation: Do one of two things and record which. Either add the missing end-to-end assertion: in the stdio/HTTP fixture path in crates/clio-mcp/tests/mcp_read_transport_conformance.rs, assert that the returned `explanation.hits[*]` key set equals the six trace keys and that no entity name appears, so the end-to-end category has its own contract. Or reword the §9 AC-100740-01 evidence to say 'in-process dispatch' and state in the Completion Evidence that the end-to-end category is covered by the pre-existing transport parity fixture, then tick the §8 checkboxes that are genuinely met and leave a reason next to the ones that are not.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED (remediation r1) by adding the missing end-to-end test (recommendation option 1). New test explain_trace_key_contract_over_stdio_and_http in crates/clio-mcp/tests/mcp_read_transport_conformance.rs runs a real retrieve with explain:true over BOTH transports (JSON-RPC frames through McpHandler on stdio; Streamable HTTP) and asserts per transport: explanation.hits non-empty, every hit's key set == the shipped TRACE_HIT_KEYS, and no entity name from the payload hits appears in the rendered trace. Output: 'test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed' for the binary; 'cargo test -p clio-mcp --locked --lib read_explain' still '6 passed; 0 failed'. Phase doc updated: AC-100740-01 evidence now distinguishes the in-process dispatch tests from this real-transport test, and all seven §8 Required Tests checkboxes are ticked with per-item evidence (they were all '- [ ]' before, while §9/DoD claimed tests pass).

findings.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/read_entities_tests.rs:357-360 documents `entity_match_never_reaches_the_explanation_trace` with 'the trace is a hand-written projection, so the exclusion is deliberate rather than a side effect of omission'. After the staged change the trace comes from the `ExplainHit` view in read_explain.rs:99-127, so the stated reason is false; the exclusion is now enforced by the projection's field list and proven by `every_hit_field_is_classified_and_matches_the_projection`. The assertion itself still holds and still passes, so this is a stale reason, not a behaviour regression. crates/clio-mcp/src/read_retrieve.rs:20 also still says 'Changes to retrieval read binding or explain shaping should normally require changes here', and line 11 still lists '`explain` trace assembly' under Owns, although per-hit shaping moved to read_explain.rs. Only the function-level doc at read_retrieve.rs:115-120 was updated.
findings.requirement_ref: AGENTS.md 'The responsibility and ownership statements MUST accurately describe the actual module'; phase doc §2 In Scope 'Updating call sites'; phase doc Definition of Done 'Documentation is updated where required'
findings.recommendation: Update the comment at read_entities_tests.rs:357-360 to name the real mechanism (the `ExplainHit` allowlist plus the classification sweep) and update the read_retrieve.rs module header so Owns says the top-level trace counters and Boundary points per-hit shaping at `crate::read_explain`. Both are comment-only edits; no test change is needed.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED (remediation r1), comment-only edits. read_entities_tests.rs:357-360 now names the real mechanism: the trace hit comes from the ExplainHit allowlist projection in read_explain, enforced by that projection's field list plus the classification sweep in read_explain_guard_tests (every_hit_field_is_classified_and_matches_the_projection). read_retrieve.rs module header now says Owns: 'explain trace assembly at the binding: the top-level counters and timings ... The per-hit shape comes from crate::read_explain' and Boundary: 'Changes to per-hit trace shaping belong in crate::read_explain'. No test changes needed; the untouched assertion still passes ('6 passed; 0 failed').

findings.title: The phase file keeps a wrong file:line citation for the conformance volatile mask as a Required Discovery fact, even though the developer run found it wrong
findings.evidence: private/clio-private/roadmap/phase-100740-explain-trace-projection.md line 46 and line 97 both cite `crates/clio-mcp/tests/mcp_read_conformance.rs:196-228` as the conformance volatile mask, and §4 'Required Discovery' plus §3 'Dependencies' tell the next agent to re-verify against it. That file is 177 lines long and contains no `mask_volatile` at all (grep for 'mask_volatile' in it returns nothing). The real masks are crates/clio-mcp/tests/mcp_read_transport_conformance.rs:146-163 (VOLATILE with 13 keys, including `score` and `metrics`, which is what the phase file describes) and crates/clio-mcp/tests/conformance.rs:327-350 (VOLATILE with 7 keys and no `score`/`metrics`). The developer's own run log records this discovery, but the phase file was not corrected. The same block also says '`read_retrieve.rs` is 271 lines' (line 49) while the file is now 274 lines.
findings.requirement_ref: phase doc §4 'Required Discovery' (agent MUST re-verify before editing) and §3 'Dependencies' Validation column
findings.recommendation: Fix the two citations in the phase file to `crates/clio-mcp/tests/mcp_read_transport_conformance.rs:146-163` (and note the separate mask in `crates/clio-mcp/tests/conformance.rs:327-350`), and update the line-49 file-size note to 274. The citation was already wrong at plan time, so any agent that trusts it will look in a file that has no mask.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED (remediation r1). Verified the finding first: mcp_read_conformance.rs is 177 lines and 'grep mask_volatile' returns nothing; the masks are mcp_read_transport_conformance.rs:146-163 (13-key VOLATILE incl. score/metrics) and conformance.rs:326-350 (7-key id-only). Phase file fixed: Design References line and the Dependencies table now cite mcp_read_transport_conformance.rs:146-163 and note the second conformance.rs:326-350 mask; the file-size note now reads 'read_retrieve.rs is 271 lines (274 after implementation; 277 after the remediation-r1 header fix)'.

findings.title: The new module's doc comment overstates compile-time enforcement and declares a key order that no test checks
findings.evidence: read_explain.rs:49-51 says 'The three tables below are the declared classification contract. They compile only for tests; production code enforces the same classification at compile time through the exhaustive pattern in `explain_hit`.' The exhaustive pattern at read_explain.rs:114-125 only forces a field to be named; `newfield: _` compiles cleanly and leaves the field unclassified (demonstrated by mutation C in F-01). read_explain.rs:56 describes `TRACE_HIT_KEYS` as 'in wire order', but every comparison treats it as an unordered set (`keys(hit)` returns a `BTreeSet<String>` at read_explain_tests.rs:60-63 and read_explain_guard_tests.rs:103-106; both assertions compare with `set_of(TRACE_HIT_KEYS)` at read_explain_tests.rs:182 and read_explain_guard_tests.rs:225). serde_json's `preserve_order` feature is not enabled anywhere in the workspace, so `Map` is a `BTreeMap` and the emitted key order is alphabetical regardless of the array order, which makes the 'wire order' note both untested and misleading.
findings.requirement_ref: AGENTS.md file-header rule: ownership statements must accurately describe the actual module
findings.recommendation: Reword read_explain.rs:49-51 to state what each mechanism really enforces (the pattern forces a field to be mentioned; the test-only sweep forces it to be classified), and change 'in wire order' on read_explain.rs:56 to 'the trace-visible hit keys' since order is neither emitted nor asserted.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED (remediation r1). read_explain.rs module doc no longer claims compile-time classification enforcement: it now states the exhaustive pattern only forces every field to be mentioned ('newfield: _' compiles) while the drift-guard sweep in read_explain_guard_tests forces every field name to be classified, and that the sweep walks struct fields by name so serde-skipped fields cannot hide. read_explain.rs:56 'in wire order' replaced with 'The key order is not part of the contract: the trace is a JSON object and neither the projection nor any assertion depends on key order.' Additionally (plan_unlimited): the three tables were promoted out of #[cfg(test)] into shipped pub constants (pub mod read_explain in lib.rs), read by the wire tests, the drift guard, and the new transport e2e test.
